questions.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to a Trigonometric Equation Containing Tangent or Cotangent
questions.problem: In degrees, find the general solution to the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}.$  Assume that $n$ is an integer.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
{x}_{1}=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})=-{30}^{∘}
$$

The tangent function has a period of ${180}^{∘}.$  Hence, the general solution for the given equation is: 

$$
x=-{30}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Coordinates of the Points of Intersection of a Trigonometric Curve and a Horizontal Line
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13994895/assets/6839910f0269266caf6888e1e921506bd9585c6805e3d787538771cf379901f7.png)

The graph shows a portion of the curve $y=\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and $y=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.$ Which of the following generates the $x$-values of all of their points of intersection? Assume that $n$ is an integer.
questions.worked_solution:
At the intersection points, the $y$-values are the same for both graphs. This gives the equation $\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.$ 

First, we find the principal value:

$$
{x}_{1}=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})={30}^{∘}
$$

Our first solution lies in the $1$st quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={30}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the fourth quadrant, and it also has ${\theta }_{R}={30}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13994895/assets/8c6e3ae6bdbfb1c66aee719f77225453992fffe6f3c6e3dfdc3f1ff92c59863a.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$  lies in the $4$th quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={360}^{∘}-{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={360}^{∘}-{30}^{∘} \\  & ={330}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the general solution for the given equation is

$$
x={30}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘},\,x={330}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Coordinates of the Points of Intersection of a Trigonometric Curve and a Horizontal Line
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13994895/assets/e4845bc1fbe702020161e15391e0c2bf8b8c2ee4fcd953790707ce5505d4df56.png)

The graph above shows a portion of the curve $y=\operatorname{sec}⁡x$ and the line $y=2.$ The expressions 

$$
x={\theta }_{1}+n\cdot b,\,x={\theta }_{2}+n\cdot b,
$$

where ${\theta }_{1}<{\theta }_{2}$ and $n$ is an integer, generate the $x$-values of all of the points of intersection. Find the values of ${\theta }_{1}$ and ${\theta }_{2}$ in $[0,{360}^{∘}),$ and the value of $b.$

${\theta }_{1}=${{field-1}}${}^{∘},\,{\theta }_{2}=$
{{field-2}}${}^{∘},\,b=$
{{field-3}}${}^{∘}$
questions.worked_solution:
At the intersection points, the $y$-values are the same for both graphs. This gives the equation

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sec}⁡x=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x},$ therefore the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

First, we find the principal value:

$$
{x}_{1}=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{1}{2})={60}^{∘}.
$$

Our first solution lies in the $1$st quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={60}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the $4$th quadrant, and it also has ${\theta }_{R}={60}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13994895/assets/40879eca8abd0b5b45d233a6aafe8642a10aaa7cf91b090bee86b47333beb0b8.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$  lies in the $4$th quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={360}^{∘}-{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={360}^{∘}-{60}^{∘} \\  & ={300}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

The general solution for the given equation is 

$$
x={60}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘},\,x=-{60}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.
$$

Writing this as $x=\theta +n\cdot {360}^{∘},$ where $\theta \in [0,{360}^{∘}),$ we get

$$
x={60}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘},\,x={300}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.
$$

Therefore, since ${\theta }_{1}<{\theta }_{2},$ we have ${\theta }_{1}=60\,{\,}^{∘},$ ${\theta }_{2}=300\,{\,}^{∘},$ and $b=360\,{\,}^{∘}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to a Trigonometric Equation Containing Secant or Cosecant
questions.problem:
Assuming that $n$ is an integer, the general solution to the equation $3\operatorname{csc}⁡x-6=0$ is given by 

$$
x={\theta }_{1}+bn,\,x={\theta }_{2}+bn,
$$

where ${\theta }_{1}<{\theta }_{2}.$ Find the values of ${\theta }_{1}$ and ${\theta }_{2}$ in $[0,2\pi ),$ and the value of $b.$

${\theta }_{1}=${{field-1}}$,\,{\theta }_{2}=$
{{field-2}}$,\,b=$
{{field-3}}
questions.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation and isolate $\operatorname{csc}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3\,\operatorname{csc}⁡x-6 & =0 \\ 3\,\operatorname{csc}⁡x & =6 \\ \operatorname{csc}⁡x & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that $\operatorname{csc}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}.$ Therefore, the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
{x}_{1}=arcsin\,(\frac{1}{2})=\frac{\pi }{6}
$$

Our first solution lies in the $1$st quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{6}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the $2$nd quadrant, and it also has ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{6}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13994895/assets/b0738a8a505b89ff687cb4de350a00f2e10d6209fbeee7dcdfdf0ee359a9cc3c.png)

Since the second solution lies in the $2$nd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi -\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

The general solution for the given equation is

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{6}+2\pi n,\,x=\frac{5\pi }{6}+2\pi n.
$$

Therefore, since ${\theta }_{1}<{\theta }_{2},$ we have ${\theta }_{1}=\frac{\pi }{6},\text{ }{\theta }_{2}=\frac{5\pi }{6},\text{ }\text{and}\text{ }b=2\pi .$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to a Trigonometric Equation Containing Tangent or Cotangent
questions.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation $\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}+2}$ in the form $x=\theta +n\cdot b$ where $\theta \in [0,{180}^{∘}),$ $n$ is an integer and $b$ is the period in degrees.

*Hint: You may use the fact that $tan\,({75}^{∘})=\sqrt{3}+2.$*

$x=$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}+\,n\,\cdot $
{{field-2}}${}^{∘}$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that $\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}.$ Therefore, the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}+2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡x & =\sqrt{3}+2.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
{x}_{1}=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{3}+2)={75}^{∘}
$$

The tangent function has a period of ${180}^{∘}.$  Hence, the general solution for the given equation is

$$
x={75}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}.
$$
